title: Auth, Session, Tenant, and Negative-Path Proof Expansion Catalogue
authorityBoundary: This catalogue is a lower-authority supporting map over the higher-authority authentication-slice proof-evidence, semantic contracts, interface/audit/event/observability instances, and source-import manifest. It records the negative-path (denial / fail-closed) coverage posture for the auth, session, and tenant slice. It defines no semantics, upgrades no readiness, and never overrides a contract, proof-evidence record, or validator. A case is only marked dev-proven when it binds to a resolving on-disk proof artefact recording the exercised negative outcome; every other case is an explicit recorded-gap or test-rung-deferred entry carrying its next rung.

cases.scenario: A non-admin tenant actor attempts a delegated-administration grant or revoke operation. Per the delegated-administration-roles contract this returns static-permission-denied with no mutation and no success audit. No on-disk proof harness exercises the RBAC role-matrix denial yet, so this is recorded as a gap rather than claimed as proven.
cases.nextRung: Author a USF hermetic RBAC role-matrix negative proof harness that exercises static-permission-denied for every non-admin role/permission pair and emits proof-evidence under evidence/proof-evidence/.

cases.scenario: The manager role, which holds only a legacy member bundle without tenant member-management permissions, attempts a tenant member-management operation. Per the user-identity-and-tenant-membership contract this is denied. Semantic definition is on disk; no exercised proof artefact is, so this is a recorded gap.
cases.nextRung: Extend the RBAC role-matrix negative proof harness to assert the manager legacy bundle cannot invoke member-management routes and emit proof-evidence.

cases.scenario: A support-mode system-admin whose effective tenant is A requests tenant B's FQDN. Per the support-mode-break-glass-access contract only the matching effective tenant's FQDN is accessible, so the cross-tenant request is denied (wrong-tenant FQDN denial). The contract sourceRefs are historical lineage not present on disk, so this is a recorded gap.
cases.nextRung: Author a hermetic support-mode wrong-tenant proof rung that binds an effective tenant A session and asserts tenant B FQDN access is denied, emitting proof-evidence.

cases.scenario: A membership in tenant A is projected onto a session actor for tenant B. Per the user-identity-and-tenant-membership contract, identity is projected only through verified membership and fails closed for other-tenant membership. Semantic definition is on disk; no exercised proof artefact is, so this is a recorded gap.
cases.nextRung: Author a hermetic membership-projection proof rung asserting an other-tenant membership yields no session actor for the requested tenant, emitting proof-evidence.

cases.scenario: The authentication login route receives a request that carries no valid authenticated session. The proof-only harness observed the no-session response outcome, minting no authenticated session and failing closed to unauthorized. An expired session token is one form of the non-valid-session refusal path this proof exercised; the explicit TTL-boundary variant is deferred to AUTH-NEG-006.

A session token exactly at and just past its time-to-live boundary is rejected. The proof harness exercised the absent/invalid session refusal but not the explicit TTL-expiry boundary, so this rung is deferred rather than claimed proven.
cases.nextRung: Add a hermetic TTL-boundary expiry proof rung exercising a token at expiry-1, expiry, and expiry+1 and emit proof-evidence under evidence/proof-evidence/.

cases.scenario: A login attempt whose provider assertion does not authenticate (an unverifiable or forged credential) yields the denied-login response outcome and mints no session. The proof-only harness observed the denied-login outcome at the login route boundary; this binds the synthetic/forged-credential denial to that exercised outcome.

A structurally valid but forged token (tampered signature, wrong issuer, or wrong audience) is rejected at signature verification. The current proof harness observes denied-login generically but does not isolate signature-verification negatives, so this rung is deferred.
cases.nextRung: Add a hermetic signature-verification negative proof rung (tampered signature, wrong issuer, wrong audience) and emit proof-evidence.

cases.scenario: A service or machine actor authenticating with an API key or personal access token attempts a browser-session-only route. Per the api-keys-personal-access-tokens contract a service actor cannot mint an interactive session, so the request is denied. No on-disk proof harness exercises service-actor route separation yet, so this is a recorded gap.
cases.nextRung: Author a hermetic service-actor negative proof rung asserting an API-key/PAT actor is denied browser-session-only routes and emit proof-evidence.

cases.scenario: A revoked API key or personal access token is presented for authentication. Per the api-keys-personal-access-tokens contract a revoked secret authenticates as no actor. Semantic definition is on disk; no exercised proof artefact is, so this is a recorded gap.
cases.nextRung: Author a hermetic revoked-credential proof rung asserting a revoked API key/PAT authenticates as no actor and emit proof-evidence.

cases.scenario: A tenant (non-operator) actor calls an operator-only support-mode or delegated-administration route. Per the support-mode and delegated-administration contracts these routes require platform-admin access, so the tenant actor is forbidden. Semantic definition is on disk; no exercised proof artefact is, so this is a recorded gap.
cases.nextRung: Author a hermetic operator-only route-guard proof rung asserting a tenant actor is forbidden from platform-admin routes and emit proof-evidence.

cases.scenario: An anonymous or unauthenticated client calls a permission-gated follow-on route rather than the anonymous login initiation route. Per the authentication-login-api interface contract, fail-closed authorization defaults deny permission-gated follow-on access without an authenticated session. Semantic definition is on disk; no exercised proof artefact isolates this route class, so this is a recorded gap.
cases.nextRung: Author a hermetic client-callable route-guard proof rung asserting anonymous access to permission-gated follow-on routes is denied while the anonymous login route remains callable, and emit proof-evidence.

cases.scenario: A tenant A actor attempts to read or write tenant B rows. Per the tenant-isolation-proof contract, row-level security yields a cross-tenant count of zero and foreign-key rejection, failing closed to no cross-tenant data. The proof sourceRefs are historical lineage not present on disk, so this is an explicit recorded gap.
cases.nextRung: Author a hermetic cross-tenant RLS negation proof rung asserting a tenant A actor observes zero tenant B rows and is rejected on cross-tenant writes, and emit proof-evidence under evidence/proof-evidence/.

cases.scenario: An untrusted, unresolved, apex, reserved, or malformed host is presented. Per the tenant-identity-record-and-fqdn contract, host resolution fails closed to a null tenant context rather than a partial or fallback tenant, so no tenant data is served. Semantic definition is on disk; no exercised proof artefact is, so this is a recorded gap.
cases.nextRung: Author a hermetic host-resolution negative proof rung asserting untrusted/unresolved hosts resolve to a null tenant context and serve no tenant data, and emit proof-evidence.

cases.scenario: The identity provider dependency fails during a login attempt. The proof-only harness observed the provider-failure response outcome, minting no session and failing closed rather than degrading open. The harness runs in hermetic-mock provider mode with no live-external-provider claim.
